author: NASASpaceflight
description:
This Week in Spaceflight covers Blue Origin’s first New Glenn booster reuse and droneship landing attempt, Dream Chaser Tenacity completing acoustic testing at Kennedy Space Center, Virgin Galactic’s Delta-class spaceplane factory progress and 2027 Purdue crewed mission, and Vast’s new astronaut flight suits plus its massive 2.9-meter Large Docking Adapter designed for Starship-scale commercial space stations and artificial gravity.

Also featured: Amazon’s Leo Aviation Antenna for in-flight gigabit internet, Globalstar acquisition, and Apple satellite partnership; Relativity Space’s Terran R tank integration and Aeon-R engine testing; Blue Origin leasing Vandenberg SLC-14 for West Coast polar launches; Impulse Space revealing Helios tug hardware; Voyager Technologies winning NASA’s seventh private astronaut mission to the ISS; NASA’s X-59 supersonic aircraft completing its first wheels-up flight; Rocket Lab unveiling the Gauss electric thruster and acquiring Mynaric for laser comms;
title: Blue Origin’s First New Glenn Booster Reuse Is Almost Here! | This Week in Spaceflight
